A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same context-bias study, with readable text, equations, figures, and results. v1 has no appendix; v2 includes extensive supplementary material and a second, substantially duplicated supplement, which was matched rather than counted as additional evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection, background-masking, UMAP, and MMD/MVD experiments on Cityscapes, Foggy Cityscapes, and CARLA.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds association measurements, additional datasets and classes, YOLOv11 results, and mitigation experiments in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the feature-discrepancy approach remain, but Section 3.2.3 adds a systematic procedure that masks individual background classes, calculates Droprate, and constructs normalized association matrices and graphs. Section 4.4 also introduces MIC-style masking during training as a mitigation intervention.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's Cityscapes, Foggy Cityscapes beta 0.02, and CARLA vehicle analysis, v2 evaluates KITTI semantic, Virtual KITTI, fog beta 0.01, and additional classes including person, rider, and bicycle. Supplementary Table 18 adds Virtual KITTI weather, lighting, and viewpoint scenarios.

E2.justification: MIC and Align and Distill were only discussed as related work in v1. v2 introduces actual comparisons involving unchanged Detectron2, MIC-augmented Detectron2, and ALDI++ in Section 4.4 and Figures 7, 10, and 11, substantially extending the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: The main 2D UMAP analysis changes from fourth-layer to fifth-layer ResNet features, and the stated MMD scaling changes from 1000 to 100. v2 also adds YOLO11x training and evaluation, masking and ALDI++ controls, and AP reporting alongside AP50. These settings preclude treating all new results as directly comparable improvements over v1.

E4.justification: v2 adds masking-mitigation and ALDI++ association analyses, tests architecture dependence using YOLOv11, and expands v1's brief CAM-correspondence claim into foreground/background heat-ratio analyses across layers and thresholds. Existing size/bin analyses are extended; the original 3D case study is retained in Supplementary Section 16.

E5.justification: Supplementary Section 9 newly reports foreground/background heat-ratio means and standard deviations, extending v1's brief correspondence statement. These describe variation in the measurements rather than uncertainty across training runs. Neither version reports training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 retains the original three-class observations but adds extensive AP/AP50, association, MMD/MVD, and YOLOv11 results. Section 4.4 newly reports a MIC foggy-validation improvement from 51.189 to 53.646. New Table 19 lists CARLA AP50 as 88.220, while Section 4.3 still repeats v1's 88.62; this discrepancy is not reconciled.

T1.justification: The probability factorizations and MMD/MVD reasoning are substantially retained. v2 adds mathematical definitions for Droprate as DET1 minus DET2 and foreground/background heat ratios as fc/f and bc/f in Supplementary Sections 10 and 9. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The claim that foreground alignment alone is insufficient remains. The abstract and conclusion now additionally claim that state-of-the-art DAOD exhibits context bias and that masking can alleviate it while improving detection accuracy. v1 explicitly left mitigation to future work.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes normalized association strength from absolute dependence, interprets associations through dataset pixel distributions, and attributes renewed ALDI++ associations to target-data training. It removes v1's single-model, restricted-class, and deferred-mitigation limitations, retains the computational-cost limitation, and acknowledges that pixel-distribution correlations were not statistically tested.

D1.justification: v2 adds the YOLO11x pretrained initialization, 100 epochs, batch size 15, SGD, cosine scheduling, KITTI image resolution, and dataset instance counts. The Detectron2 recipe remains. However, v1's explicit true-positive-only CAM restriction and numerical small/medium object-size boundaries are no longer documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on Virtual KITTI, augmented driving data, context in object detection, and causal reasoning, while removing the ResNet reference. Most related-work discussion and the claimed gap concerning context bias across domains remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The overall introduction–related work–methods–experiments narrative and much existing prose remain. v2 edits wording, shortens the title, adds Asma Almutairi to the author list, subdivides the methods section, makes the conclusion standalone, and adds supplementary navigation.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the main-text violin grids with numerical tables, expands UMAP displays, and adds association heatmaps and graphs. The 3D visualization moves to the supplement, which includes enlarged plots and many new tables. A substantially duplicated supplement with review headers introduces considerable redundant layout.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly limited its main quantification to one detector and three vehicle classes and deferred mitigation. v2 substantially addresses these weaknesses through broader domain/class coverage, YOLOv11 analysis, quantitative association checks, and MIC/ALDI++ experiments. This strengthens empirical support and practical relevance. The duplicated supplement, omitted implementation disclosures, and unresolved metric/result inconsistencies reduce clarity and auditability, but do not outweigh these substantive gains.
